title: Apple abandons CSAM client-side scanning plan
summary: Apple scrapped its planned on-device CSAM photo-scanning system; in later correspondence (Aug 2023) it detailed that client-side scanning cannot be built without imperiling all users' security and privacy — the central technical precedent cited against EU Chat Control.

title: Threema signs open letter: 'Data privacy is more important than ever'
summary: Swiss secure messenger Threema publicly opposed the CSA Regulation, arguing that scanning end-to-end encrypted content requires a backdoor/client-side scanning that endangers everyone's security.

title: 500+ cryptographers and security researchers reject client-side scanning
summary: Over 500 scientists with cryptography and IT-security credentials published an open letter warning that the EU CSA Regulation's client-side scanning is technically infeasible, ineffective, and a dangerous mass-surveillance precedent.

title: Tech industry open letter against mandatory scanning (Element, Proton, Threema, Tuta, Nextcloud)
actor: Element / Matrix and 18 European tech companies
summary: Eighteen European technology companies urged EU Member States to align with Parliament's position, rejecting client-side scanning and backdoors that would force mass surveillance and undermine end-to-end encryption.

title: Signal's Whittaker: 'upload moderation' is just rebranded mass scanning
summary: Reacting to the Council's E2EE proposal, Whittaker said there is no way to implement it without fundamentally undermining encryption: 'Whether you call it a backdoor, a front door, or upload moderation it undermines encryption and creates significant vulnerabilities.'

title: TechCrunch explainer: 'Chat control' — the EU's controversial CSAM-scanning proposal
summary: In-depth tech-press explainer of the CSA Regulation, detailing how client-side scanning would analyze content before encryption and require real-time grooming detection, and why critics call it mass surveillance.

title: EU Perspectives: 'EU Chat Control heads for a decisive vote'
summary: Tracker-quality coverage framing the Danish presidency's push and the looming October Council vote on mandatory detection orders.

title: Euronews: 'Return of chat control — something is rotten in the state of Denmark'
summary: Quality-journalism analysis of the Danish Council Presidency reviving Chat Control from July 2025, categorizing services into low/medium/high risk and pushing client-side scanning toward an October vote.

title: Tuta: 'We will not stand by while the EU destroys encryption'
summary: German encrypted-email provider Tuta declared it would exit the European market rather than compromise user security and signaled readiness to litigate if Chat Control's scanning mandate passes.

title: Scientists renew open letter warning against Danish Chat Control text
actor: CSA Scientist Open Letter (500+ researchers, 34 countries)
summary: Cryptographers and security researchers issued an updated statement calling the Danish presidency's proposal 'technically infeasible,' a 'danger to democracy,' and a direct threat to the privacy of all EU citizens.

title: Signal threatens to leave the EU market; urges Germany to vote No
summary: Whittaker called on Germany to reject Chat Control, saying that faced with a choice between undermining its encryption guarantees or leaving Europe, Signal 'would make the decision to leave the market.'

title: Germany joins blocking minority, killing the October Council vote
summary: Germany, alongside Luxembourg and others, formed a blocking minority representing over 35% of the EU population, forcing withdrawal of the planned 14 October vote on mandatory scanning.

title: Euronews: 'Chat Control on hold, Europe's Eastern flank remains passive'
summary: Analysis of the postponed October vote, the blocking minority, and how Eastern EU member states largely stayed passive in the debate.

title: Netherlands rejects Chat Control proposal over encryption threat
summary: The Dutch Justice Minister told parliament the Netherlands would not support mandatory scanning that threatens secure, private digital communication, weakening Council support.

title: Max Planck Society: 'More monitoring, but not more protection'
actor: Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy (Carmela Troncoso)
summary: Max Planck welcomed removal of mandatory scanning but warned that expanded 'voluntary' monitoring (now text and video) plus mandatory age verification create privacy risks without demonstrable child-protection benefits.

title: EU Perspectives: Breyer warns heavy lifting moves into 2026
summary: Coverage of the Council's 26 November general approach kicking off trilogue negotiations, with former MEP Patrick Breyer warning the decisive fight would continue into 2026.

title: EFF: 'Chat Control nears its final hurdle — what to know'
summary: EFF argued that even without mandatory scanning, 'voluntary' scanning plus broad risk-mitigation and age-verification mandates would undermine privacy, and urged that client-side scanning be explicitly ruled incompatible with encryption.

title: EU Perspectives: Parliament committee votes down CSAM-scanning extension
summary: Tech-press tracker reporting the parliamentary rejection of extending the 'voluntary' Chat Control 1.0 derogation, leading to expiry of the interim regulation on 4 April 2026.

title: closednetwork.io live tracker of the Chat Control fight
summary: Continuously updated live tracker documenting every Council vote, blocking minority, and trilogue on Chat Control; last updated 30 June 2026 noting the fifth/final trilogue under the Cyprus presidency.

title: MEP Martin Sonneborn: fast-track Chat Control 'suspends a fundamental right'
summary: At the Strasbourg plenary, Sonneborn challenged the urgency procedure, brandished the rulebook demanding the motion be ruled inadmissible, and said the derogation 'suspends a fundamental right, the confidentiality of telecommunications' — his mic was cut after 60 seconds.

title: EU Perspectives: Parliament forced back to the Chat Control question
summary: MEPs narrowly approved (331-304) scheduling a Thursday revote on extending the scanning derogation via urgent procedure; Green MEP Markéta Gregorová accused proponents of abusing Parliament's rules.
